newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says baht at 30/dlr appropriate.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says baht at 30/dlr appropriate.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said that it considered the baht at 30 to the dollar as an appropriate level for the currency which was floated on July 2 and sank to a new record low on Monday

Deputy Bank of Thailand Governor Chaiyawat Wibulsawasdi told a news conference that the baht had on Monday fallen to a level that it believed was low enough. It would take action to stabilise the currency and stop any more wild fluctuations.

The baht tumbled to a new record low of 30.30/30.75 against the dollar on commercial sales of the dollar and on sustained jitters in the market about the Philippines peso and other regional currencies, dealers said.

The baht steadied after the central bank statement to around 29.50/30.00. Dealers also speculated earlier in the day that the central bank may have intervened by selling dollars into the market to stem the currency's sharp fall on Monday.

"The baht has been falling sharply against the dollar recently to around 30 baht which is already at a very low level. The central bank thinks that it is at an appropriate level already," Chaiyawat said.
"The baht has fallen by 15 pct since the new foreign exchange regime was introduced and the central bank thinks it is already at a level that is too low," he added.
He based the 15 percent fall on Monday's reference rate for the baht that was announced at 29.945 per dollar against 29.155 on Friday.
"It is our direct responsibility to take measures to do anything that will help stabilise the foreign exchange rate and ease volatility in the market," he said.
Thai authorities changed the baht system to a managed float system on July 2 after pegging it for 13 years to a trade weighted basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
